findings.reason: TrieUtils.ts:33-40 shows the three new @ts-expect-error directives on iter.size reads/writes and iter.__iterate. The base interface Collection at immutable.d.ts:4351 doesn't declare them. Line 36 covers two errors with one directive. New suppressions instead of fixes count as findings under L5.4.
findings.claim: ensureSize types iter as Collection<unknown, unknown> and adds three @ts-expect-error suppressions instead of a type that describes size/__iterate, so its core logic goes unchecked.
findings.evidence: ensureSize types `iter` as `Collection<unknown, unknown>`. The base `interface Collection<K, V>` in type-definitions/immutable.d.ts:4351 declares neither `size` nor `__iterate`, so every access needs a suppression: line 34 `if (iter.size === undefined)`, line 36 for `iter.size = iter.__iterate(returnTrue)`, and line 39 `return iter.size`. The comment on line 36 admits it covers two separate errors ("size should exists..., __iterate does exist"), so a single directive hides any error on that line. A local type such as `{ size?: number; __iterate(fn): number }` would avoid all three suppressions.

findings.reason: TrieUtils.ts:72 and :91 test end/index === undefined. wrapIndex keeps a typeof index !== 'number' branch (54-60). The JS callers (List.js:185, Range.js:77, Operations.js:411, Stack.js:118) pass the user's possibly undefined slice end straight through, and tsconfig has strict: true. Runtime behaviour is unchanged because the callers are still JS, so it stays low.
findings.claim: New signatures (wholeSlice, resolveBegin/End, resolveIndex, wrapIndex, SetRef) declare plain number/Ref while bodies and callers handle undefined or string inputs.
findings.evidence: `wholeSlice(begin: number, end: number, size: number)` and `resolveIndex(index: number, size: number, ...)` take plain `number`, yet the bodies test `end === undefined`, `size !== undefined` and `index === undefined`. Callers like List.js:185, Range.js:77 and Operations.js:411 pass through the user's `slice(begin, end)` arguments, and `end` is often undefined. `wrapIndex(iter, index: number)` (line 43) keeps a `typeof index !== 'number'` branch (lines 54-60) that parses string indexes, but under the declared type that branch narrows `index` to `never`. `SetRef(ref: Ref)` is non-optional but still guards `if (ref)`. tsconfig.json sets `strict: true`, so these types should be `number | undefined`, `number | string` and `Ref | undefined`.

findings.reason: diff.patch shows four comment-only hunks in deepEqual.ts that change 'size exists' to 'size should exists' with no code change. deepEqual.ts doesn't depend on the TrieUtils typing, so these are unrequested changes (L4.27). Cosmetic only.
findings.claim: The diff rewords four existing suppression comments in deepEqual.ts, which the TrieUtils conversion doesn't need, and introduces a grammar error ('should exists').
findings.evidence: Four hunks swap `// @ts-expect-error size exists on Collection` for `// @ts-expect-error size should exists on Collection` without changing any code. deepEqual.ts only imports `NOT_SET` from '../TrieUtils', and nothing in it depends on the rename.
